statement_record.book: Six claims. Set-level: A × (B + C) ≅ (A×B) + (A×C), (B×C)^A ≅ B^A × C^A, A^{B+C} ≅ A^B × A^C, each because A × − and A^{(−)} are adjoints. Cardinal-level: the corresponding equations α(β+γ) = αβ+αγ, (βγ)^α = β^α γ^α, α^{β+γ} = α^β α^γ, obtained by pushing the natural isomorphisms through the cardinality functor |−| : Set_iso ⟶ Card into the discrete category of cardinals.
statement_record.intree: All three set-level isomorphisms are proved, and proved in greater generality — for an arbitrary bicartesian closed category rather than Set: `prod_coprod_r : x × (y + z) ≅ x × y + x × z`, `exp_prod_r : (y × z)^x ≅ y^x × z^x`, `exp_coprod : x^(y + z) ≅ x^y × x^z`. They instantiate at Sets (Sets_Cartesian / Sets_Cocartesian / Sets_Closed) and at Coq (Coq_Cartesian / Coq_Cocartesian / Coq_Closed). Theory/Algebra.v collects them as an index of categorified high-school algebra, but does so with anonymous `Goal … auto. Qed.` statements, so the named instances above are the real assertions. No cardinal arithmetic exists.

statement_record.book: For any adjoint pair between abelian categories, the left adjoint is right exact (preserves finite colimits), the right adjoint is left exact (preserves finite limits), and BOTH functors are additive, i.e. preserve finite direct sums (a finite direct sum being simultaneously a finite limit and a finite colimit).
statement_record.intree: The two exactness clauses hold a fortiori and unconditionally: `right_adjoint_preserves_limits : PreservesAllLimits U` and `left_adjoint_preserves_colimits : PreservesAllColimits F` for every adjunction F ⊣ U, over arbitrary index categories and with no abelian hypothesis. evidence.intree_statement: Record Reflective {C : Category} (S : Subcategory C) := { reflective_full : Construction.Subcategory.Full C S; reflector : C ⟶ Sub C S; reflective_adj : reflector ⊣ Incl C S }.
Lemma reflective_counit_iso {C : Category} {S : Subcategory C} (R : Reflective S) (x : Sub C S) : reflector R (Incl C S x) ≅[Sub C S] x.
Theorem reflector_inverts_W {a b : C} (w : a ~> b) (Hw : W a b w) : IsIsomorphism (fmap[Refl] w).   (* Refl := reflector R for a Reflective (C_W W), the full subcategory of W-local objects *)

statement_record.book: A reflective subcategory of C is a full subcategory D whose inclusion D ↪ C admits a LEFT adjoint L, the reflector or localization. Identifying D with its image, the unit components are η_c : c → Lc and, by Lemma 4.6.11(iii), the counit components ε_d : Ld → d are isomorphisms — every object of a reflective subcategory is naturally isomorphic to its reflection. The dual notion, coreflective subcategory (inclusion has a right adjoint), is named in the surrounding prose.
statement_record.intree: `Record Reflective (S : Subcategory C)` bundles exactly the book's three data: fullness of the subcategory (`reflective_full`), the reflector `reflector : C ⟶ Sub C S`, and the adjunction `reflective_adj : reflector ⊣ Incl C S`. The counit-iso consequence Riehl derives from 4.6.11(iii) is proved as `reflective_counit_iso : reflector R (Incl C S x) ≅[Sub C S] x`, with the counit as the forward map and the fullness-lifted unit as its inverse. The dual is `Coreflective S := @Reflective (C^op) (op_subcategory S)` (Construction/Reflective.v:85). The 'localization' reading is made a theorem in Construction/Localization.v: the reflector onto the full subcategory of W-local objects inverts every W-morphism (`reflector_inverts_W`), with the universal property in Construction/Localization/Universal.v.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same — the definition matches clause for clause (full subcategory, left adjoint to the inclusion, named reflector), the counit-iso remark is proved rather than assumed, and the coreflective dual is present. The in-tree version does NOT identify D with its image (Sub C S is a genuine subcategory construction rather than a suppressed inclusion), which is a presentational difference only; if anything it is more explicit than the book.
